feeds.title: Simply Emma
feeds.description: Simply Emma - one of the leading disability bloggers providing comprehensive reviews & advice on accessible travel. The blog was created to encourage others, with or without a disability, to travel more and make new discoveries, whether that's abroad or in their own hometown. It covers personal stories with accessible travel guides, accommodation reviews, live event reviews, travel tips, and resources.

feeds.title: Disabled Motoring UK Magazine
feeds.description: Disabled Motoring UK is a campaigning charity for disabled drivers, passengers and Blue Badge holders. The magazine includes information on our current campaigns, the latest news and reviews of vehicles, scooters and mobility aids as well as features on everything from accessible holidays to vehicle reviews.

feeds.title: Hannah's Hope
feeds.description: My name is Hannah and I am 30 years old. I suffer from several illnesses and as a result, I am disabled and use a powerchair. I am very determined. I hope to get myself as independent and 'well' as possible. Hope keeps me going hence why 'Hannah's Hope' seemed an appropriate title for my blog!

feeds.title: H W Mobility Blog
feeds.description: We are Andrew & Julie and we've been in the mobility furniture industry for a combined 22 years and counting. We use only the finest designers and manufacturers throughout the United Kingdom. Our blog page consists of articles written by us and by guest bloggers near and far.

feeds.title: Left Brain Right Brain
feeds.description: Left Brain/Right Brain first came into existence in 2003. Over the years it has changed its basic form a few times but its core content and interest has always been autism and the news, science - and bad science associated with it.

feeds.title: Disabled Living Blog
feeds.description: Disabled Living is a charity which provides impartial information and advice about products, equipment (assistive technology) and services for disabled adults, children, older people, carers and the professionals who support them.

feeds.title: Wheel Life Blog
feeds.description: Follow this blog where Elaine shares her journey of disability issues and her view at life from a wheelchair.

feeds.title: Shona Louise
feeds.description: Shona started her blog back in 2011 and writes about her experience with Marfan Syndrome as well as other conditions, including chronic pain. Having started blogging at an early age, Shona has grown up in the blogging community and has recently spoken about the effectiveness of single-use plastic for those with disabilities. She raises awareness in ways that able-bodied people may not have seen before, making her blog unique and helpful for those in all walks of life.

feeds.title: Carrie-Ann Lightley Disabled Travel Blogger
feeds.description: Carrie-Ann Lightley is a disabled travel expert, blogger and writer. Get Accessible tourism advice, expertise and inspiration from Carrie-Ann Lightley. Disabled travel expert, blogger and writer since 2005.

feeds.title: David Ventures
feeds.description: Disability Sports Writer & Motivational Speaker. I was born with Cerebral Palsy but never let my disability prevent me from participating in outdoor pursuits, achieving my goals and fulfilling my potential. And now through writing, motivational speaking and mentoring I share my experience that thoughts that can't help but motivate and inspire others.

feeds.title: Neo-Walk Blog
feeds.description: Hear about my experiences as an above knee amputee and how designing and making walking sticks is so fulfilling and challenging.

feeds.title: London Disability
feeds.description: Applying for disability benefits in Maryland can be difficult & stressful. London disability lawyers & advocates are here to help guide you through the entire process. Read the trending updates, news and blog posts about SSDI, SSD benefits and SSI.

feeds.title: The Disability Sports Network
feeds.description: I am new to Disabled Sports, but not new to sports photography, I have been covering watersports eg Sailing, windsurfing, etc. Now that I am disabled, I need to change my direction and be more sedentary about my photography, hence myself delving into disabled sports, and I have some new ideas I want to try out if you will let me.
